precepts.text: He transgresseth by wine, his philosophies and policies (Micah 2:11, prophesying of wine and strong drink is the spirit of falsehood); he is a proud man, none prouder than Trump; keepeth not at home but is in Venezuela and Iran; enlargeth his desire as hell, and wherever he sets up democracy the place goes to hell; is as death and cannot be satisfied, now wanting Greenland and Canada; and gathereth unto him all nations, the melting pot. Shall not all these, the remnants from the destabilized countries living here, take up a taunting proverb: woe to him that increaseth that which is not his, how long? He seized Russia's boats and wealth too. Shall they not rise up suddenly that shall bite thee, sleeper cells from Nigeria, Somalia, Yemen, and Iran, because thou hast spoiled many nations, because of men's blood. Bomb a school of five-to-ten-year-old girls and their fathers and cousins here will not let bygones be bygones; that is how you make a terrorist.
precepts.point: When thou shalt cease to spoil, thou shalt be spoiled, and when thou makest an end to deal treacherously, they shall deal treacherously with thee. God will let the nations rise up.
precepts.why:
Habakkuk draws the spoiler of Isaiah 33:1 line by line. “Yea also, because he transgresseth by wine”: this white man transgresses by wine, and his wine is his philosophies, his falsehoods, his political policies and his religions. “he is a proud man”: you don't get no prouder than this white man, in particular Donald Trump. “neither keepeth at home”: America don't keep at home; he's in everybody's business. What are you doing in Venezuela? What are you doing over there in Iran?

“who enlargeth his desire as hell”: wherever he goes he sets up democracy, and that country, city or state goes to hell, a low state. God says he “is as death, and cannot be satisfied”. He steals one thing and still ain't satisfied; now he wants Denmark, and says he should take Canada too. God is showing us this man's attributes. He “gathereth unto him all nations, and heapeth unto him all people”: America is the great melting pot, all nations, languages and tongues are here.

“Shall not all these take up a parable against him, and a taunting proverb against him, and say, Woe to him that increaseth that which is not his! how long?” All these are the remnants from the destabilized, bombed and devastated countries, and they are here now. The oil in Venezuela is not his, the riches in Iran are not his, the riches of Libya he took; when he put sanctions on Russia they seized Russia's boats and all the wealth Putin had in American places, and nobody says nothing. How long is this going to go on? The thick clay he ladeth himself with is the nations he has all around him, the ones that come to live in America and say, I love Donald.

“Shall they not rise up suddenly that shall bite thee, and awake that shall vex thee”: awake from sleep, because they are sleeper cells from the nations he destroyed. They bombed Nigeria, and you got Nigerians here; they bombed Somalia, and you got a whole lot of Somalis here; Yemen, and you got Yemenites; they've been hitting Iran, and a lot of Iranians live in the United States.

“Because thou hast spoiled many nations, all the remnant of the people shall spoil thee; because of men’s blood”. You murdered civilians, innocent men, innocent women, innocent children. You killed my mother, my father, my son, my daughter: that's how you make a terrorist. The first thing they bombed in Iran was a school full of little girls ages 5 to 10. Their mothers and fathers are screaming and crying, their relatives here are asking what happened to their little cousins, and there's no forgiveness for that. They are not going to let bygones be bygones.

That is Isaiah 33:1 fulfilled: the one that spoiled and was not spoiled shall be spoiled, by the very remnant of the nations he robbed.

precepts.text: If a man walking in the spirit and falsehood do lie, saying I will prophesy unto thee of wine and strong drink, he shall even be the prophet of this people. Wine is the metaphor for the spirit of falsehood and lies.
precepts.point: When thou shalt cease to spoil, thou shalt be spoiled, and when thou makest an end to deal treacherously, they shall deal treacherously with thee. God will let the nations rise up.
precepts.why:
“If a man walking in the spirit and falsehood do lie, saying, I will prophesy unto thee of wine and of strong drink; he shall even be the prophet of this people.” This defines the wine of Habakkuk 2:5. Wine is a metaphor for the spirit of falsehood and lies.

So when Habakkuk says the spoiler “transgresseth by wine”, it is not speaking of a drunkard. This white man transgresses by his falsehoods: his philosophies, his political policies, his religions. That is the wine he prophesies, and he makes himself the prophet of the people with it.

That is the one in Isaiah 33:1 that spoils and deals treacherously: proud, in everybody's business, setting up his democracy wherever he goes. Isaiah 33:1 says woe to him, because when he ceases to spoil, he shall be spoiled.

precepts.text: When they shall say peace and safety, then sudden destruction cometh upon them, as travail upon a woman with child, and they shall not escape. When they think they have subdued the earth, it comes; birthing pains, one thing today, another in two or three months or years.
precepts.point: When thou shalt cease to spoil, thou shalt be spoiled, and when thou makest an end to deal treacherously, they shall deal treacherously with thee. God will let the nations rise up.
precepts.why:
The New Testament speaks of the same thing. “For when they shall say, Peace and safety; then sudden destruction cometh upon them”. They are going to think it's all good: we have subdued the earth, everything is ours. And the Lord says no; when you say that, then comes sudden destruction.

“as travail upon a woman with child” means birthing pains. One thing may happen today, it may calm down, and two to three months later something else happens, or it might be two to three years later. It comes like a woman giving birth. “and they shall not escape.”

That is the end of Isaiah 33:1: “when thou shalt cease to spoil, thou shalt be spoiled; and when thou shalt make an end to deal treacherously, they shall deal treacherously with thee.” When America stops robbing countries, it is going to be robbed; the nations shall deal treacherously with it, and it will come right when it says peace and safety.

precepts.text: In the fulness of his sufficiency he shall be in straits; every hand of the wicked shall come upon him, as Habakkuk 2 and Revelation 17 when NATO turns; when he is about to fill his belly God shall cast the fury of his wrath upon him and rain it upon him while he is eating. Same as Thessalonians. They try to make us the bad guys, but the real bad guys are written in the Bible, and their friends will turn on them.
precepts.point: When thou shalt cease to spoil, thou shalt be spoiled, and when thou makest an end to deal treacherously, they shall deal treacherously with thee. God will let the nations rise up.
precepts.why:
“In the fulness of his sufficiency he shall be in straits”. When he is full, because he did all the destruction and robbed the nations, he shall be in straits, meaning he is going to catch hell. This is talking about the same thing as Isaiah 33:1.

“every hand of the wicked shall come upon him.” We read that in Habakkuk 2, where all the remnant of the people shall spoil him, and you can read it in Revelation 17, when NATO turns on them, because it is going to happen.

“When he is about to fill his belly, God shall cast the fury of his wrath upon him, and shall rain it upon him while he is eating.” That is the same thing Thessalonians said: when they say peace and safety, sudden destruction.

They are trying to make it look like we are the bad guys. But the real bad guys are written in the Bible, and it is the people they are friends with now, the other nations and their own people, that are going to turn on them and attack them. The Lord told us to wait upon him till the day that he rises up. We trust in our God.

precepts.text: Let him that glorieth glory in this, that he understandeth and knoweth me, that I exercise lovingkindness, judgment, and righteousness in the earth.
precepts.point: The fear of the Lord is all wisdom, Sirach 19:20, and in all wisdom is the performance of the law: be about it, not just talk about it. If you do not fear the Lord, that is where your problems are.
precepts.why:
“O Lord, be gracious unto us; we have waited for thee”: that is our prayer, just like Hezekiah prayed. We have to wait on the Lord. “The Lord is exalted; for he dwelleth on high: he hath filled Zion with judgment and righteousness.”

Jeremiah 9:24 shows what Israel glories in: “But let him that glorieth glory in this, that he understandeth and knoweth me, that I am the Lord which exercise lovingkindness, judgment, and righteousness, in the earth: for in these things I delight, saith the Lord.” That is what we have to glory in, brothers: that we understand and know the Lord.

All nations do not understand and know the Lord, so they do not glory in the Lord. The judgment and righteousness the Lord delights to exercise in the earth are the same judgment and righteousness he has filled Zion with. Knowing him is Israel's glory, while the nations are scattered at the lifting up of himself.

precepts.text: I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, Christ, and a King shall reign and prosper and execute judgment and justice in the earth.
precepts.point: The fear of the Lord is all wisdom, Sirach 19:20, and in all wisdom is the performance of the law: be about it, not just talk about it. If you do not fear the Lord, that is where your problems are.
precepts.why:
How has the Lord “filled Zion with judgment and righteousness”? Jeremiah 23:5: “Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth.”

This righteous Branch is Christ. He is the King who shall reign and prosper, and he is the one who executes judgment and justice in the earth. So when Isaiah 33:5 says “The Lord is exalted; for he dwelleth on high: he hath filled Zion with judgment and righteousness”, it is through Christ, the King, the King of kings.

That is our hope amid destruction. When the Lord rises up, the nations are scattered and their spoil is gathered like the gathering of the caterpillar, and the righteous Branch of David reigns over Zion with judgment and justice.

precepts.text: The Lord shall smite thee with madness, blindness, and astonishment of heart. Our people are mentally unstable and spiritually blind, always shocked at the world.
precepts.point: The fear of the Lord is all wisdom, Sirach 19:20, and in all wisdom is the performance of the law: be about it, not just talk about it. If you do not fear the Lord, that is where your problems are.
precepts.why:
“And wisdom and knowledge shall be the stability of thy times.” Why is that important? The wisdom and knowledge of this Bible keeps us mentally and spiritually stable. Deuteronomy 28:28 shows the opposite: “The Lord shall smite thee with madness, and blindness, and astonishment of heart.”

Madness: our people are crazy, mentally unstable, mentally insane. Blindness: we are spiritually blind. Astonishment of heart: our people are always shocked at what is going on in the world.

That is the curse that wisdom answers. Brothers, we all need the wisdom of God and the knowledge to keep us mentally and spiritually stable. The people who know the Bible are not shocked when these things happen, because the Bible already said it; the people without it are astonished at every turn.

precepts.text: The fear of the Lord is all wisdom, and in all wisdom is the performance of the law, and the knowledge of his omnipotency.
precepts.point: The fear of the Lord is all wisdom, Sirach 19:20, and in all wisdom is the performance of the law: be about it, not just talk about it. If you do not fear the Lord, that is where your problems are.
precepts.why:
“the fear of the Lord is his treasure.” Sirach 19:20 says “The fear of the Lord is all wisdom; and in all wisdom is the performance of the law, and the knowledge of his omnipotency.”

So the fear of the Lord is all wisdom. Brothers and sisters, if you don't fear the Lord, that is where your problems are.

And in all wisdom is the performance of the law: the application of God's law. We must not just talk about it; we must be about it. We must do it. The wisdom and knowledge that are the stability of our times are not only words in the head; they are the law performed, joined to the knowledge of his omnipotency. That is the treasure the Lord loves.

precepts.text: Having eyes full of adultery, that cannot cease from sin, beguiling unstable souls, cursed children. The flip side of stability: a mind not saturated with the word. We all have children we train up, and Samuel's went to hell; you will find out which spirits serve the Lord.
precepts.point: The fear of the Lord is all wisdom, Sirach 19:20, and in all wisdom is the performance of the law: be about it, not just talk about it. If you do not fear the Lord, that is where your problems are.
precepts.why:
Wisdom and knowledge are the stability of our times. 2 Peter 2:14 is the flip side of that, what it looks like when your life is not stable and your mind is not saturated with the word of God: “Having eyes full of adultery, and that cannot cease from sin; beguiling unstable souls: an heart they have exercised with covetous practices; cursed children.”

Our people have eyes full of adultery and cannot cease from sin. They beguile unstable souls, the ones without the stability of the word. Our people are cursed children.

Many of us have children, and we all want them to walk right with the Lord. We train them up the best we can, just like the prophet Samuel, yet Samuel's sons went to hell off. Be mindful, especially the women: you have to know the spirits in your children. You are going to find out which ones serve the Lord and which ones don't.

precepts.text: If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, in faith, nothing wavering; a double-minded man is unstable in all his ways. Some cannot discern why an adulterer was put out of the school. Pray for wisdom and discernment, but give the Lord something to work with: 2 Esdras 14:40, when Ezra drank, wisdom grew and his spirit strengthened his memory, because the Spirit needed a memory to access to rewrite the books. If the Bible is closed six days a week there is nothing in there for the Spirit to bring to mind. Views peak on Sabbath and nobody watches the rest of the week, the same as Christians on Sunday; many are called, few are chosen. Let the brother of low degree rejoice that he is exalted: the quiet brother who studies and prays becomes the one breaking down scripture years later. Sirach 11:12, the slow man wanting ability, the eye of the Lord looked upon him for good and set him up from his low estate. Put on Bible audio at night if reading hurts your eyes.
precepts.point: The fear of the Lord is all wisdom, Sirach 19:20, and in all wisdom is the performance of the law: be about it, not just talk about it. If you do not fear the Lord, that is where your problems are.
precepts.why:
“If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.” If any of you are dumb as a rock, ask of God. Some do not have the spirit of discernment: they see right and wrong in front of them and cannot discern it. When judgment is passed there is always that one who asks why a brother or sister had to be put out of the school when all they did was commit a little adultery. Shut up and sit down; they cannot discern. So pray, as Hezekiah laid his prayer before the Lord: pray for wisdom, knowledge and the spirit of discernment.

“But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering.” And give the Lord something to work with. You cannot sit at the table with a chicken leg in one hand and a steak in the other praying, Lord, help me lose weight. Likewise you pray for wisdom but the Bible is closed Sunday through Friday and opened only on the Sabbath. The views on the classes peak on Saturday and nobody watches the rest of the week, the same as Christians on Sunday. Many are called, few are chosen; this is for the chosen few that know what to do.

“For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed.” “A double minded man is unstable in all his ways”: not some of his ways, all of them. Reading once a week leaves nothing for the Lord to work with.

“Let the brother of low degree rejoice in that he is exalted.” That brother is studying, reading and praying, Lord help my understanding, even when he does not understand yet. The quiet brother who did not do much talking years back becomes the one breaking down what the scriptures mean. If reading hurts your eyes, put on Bible audio at night and wake up to the scriptures.

precepts.text: I took it and drank, and my heart uttered understanding, wisdom grew in my breast, and my spirit strengthened my memory.
precepts.point: The fear of the Lord is all wisdom, Sirach 19:20, and in all wisdom is the performance of the law: be about it, not just talk about it. If you do not fear the Lord, that is where your problems are.
precepts.why:
When the books of Jerusalem were burned, the Lord told Ezra not to worry, and gave him the cup: “And I took it, and drank: and when I had drunk of it, my heart uttered understanding, and wisdom grew in my breast, for my spirit strengthened my memory.”

That last part is the point. God needed something to work with. The Spirit had to access Ezra's memory so that he could rewrite the records. It is like the movie Limitless: the pill opened his memory all the way back, so he could remember things he had only glanced at.

So if you do not read the Bible except on the Sabbath and you pray, Lord, open my wisdom, the Spirit comes and there is nothing in there: no memory to access and bring to your mind. Wisdom and knowledge can only be the stability of your times if the word has been put in you first, so give the Lord something to work with.

precepts.text: There is another that is slow, wanting ability and full of poverty; yet the eye of the Lord looked upon him for good and set him up from his low estate and lifted up his head from misery, so that many marvelled.
precepts.point: The fear of the Lord is all wisdom, Sirach 19:20, and in all wisdom is the performance of the law: be about it, not just talk about it. If you do not fear the Lord, that is where your problems are.
precepts.why:
For the brother who says he has a reading impediment, or that his eyes hurt: “Again, there is another that is slow, and hath need of help, wanting ability, and full of poverty.” This is a brother who is mentally slow, lacking ability, and poor.

“yet the eye of the Lord looked upon him for good, and set him up from his low estate”. The Lord lifted his head from misery, so that many who saw it marveled. It is the same as James's brother of low degree who rejoices that he is exalted.

So it is not impossible, but give the Lord something to work with. Show him that you believe and have faith, and he can do wonders. If you want to lose weight, get in the gym, eat smaller portions, walk around the block once, then twice, and let the Lord do the rest. Instead of five pieces of chicken, eat one; you won't die. In the same way, put on Bible audio if reading is hard. Do your part and the eye of the Lord will look upon you for good.

precepts.text: Signs in the sun, moon, and stars, blood moons and eclipses; distress of nations with perplexity, confusion: they say Venezuela was drug dealers and Iraq had weapons of mass destruction, but Maduro, Gaddafi, and Iran sold oil outside the dollar; when white people say it is complex, it is simple and they do not want you to know. Men's hearts failing them for fear, but not us, because wisdom is our stability; the powers of heaven, America, England, France, Germany, shall be shaken; then the Son of man in a cloud. Look up, for your redemption draweth nigh. But one word in the verse, perplexity, is Jacob's trouble; the great tribulation comes before he returns, so do not say he might come tomorrow.
precepts.point: The fear of the Lord is all wisdom, Sirach 19:20, and in all wisdom is the performance of the law: be about it, not just talk about it. If you do not fear the Lord, that is where your problems are.
precepts.why:
Luke 21 shows people who are unstable in all their ways, wavering like the waves of the sea. “And there shall be signs in the sun, and in the moon, and in the stars”: eclipses of the sun, lunar eclipses, what they call blood moons. “and upon the earth distress of nations, with perplexity”: we are living in that time now. Perplexity means confusion. They said Venezuela was drug dealers, as they did with Manuel Noriega; they said Iraq had weapons of mass destruction and did not find one bomb. Anytime white people say it is a complex issue, it is something very easy that they don't want you to know: Maduro was selling his oil in foreign currencies, not the United States dollar; Iran was doing the same; Gaddafi wanted to.

“Men’s hearts failing them for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth.” Why are they afraid? We are not afraid, because wisdom and knowledge are the stability of our times: this is what the Bible was talking about, while everybody else is confused. “for the powers of heaven shall be shaken”: America, England, France, Germany.

“And then shall they see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory. And when these things begin to come to pass, then look up, and lift up your heads; for your redemption draweth nigh.” It is going to be almost time to go home.

But there is more to the one word perplexity: it goes into Jacob's trouble, the great tribulation that comes to try us. People want to skip the tribulation and say, war, Christ might come back tomorrow. No he won't. Jacob's trouble has to come to pass first.

precepts.text: Immediately after the tribulation of those days, the stars, missiles, fall from heaven and the powers of the heavens, the European nations, are shaken with war; and then the sign of the Son of man, and he sends his angels to gather his elect, Israel, Isaiah 45:4, not Baptists, Pentecostals, Muslims, or Catholics. Isaiah 34:4-5 shows the heaven that is dissolved and rolled together like a scroll, nuclear bombs, with the host falling like leaves and satellites dropping: my sword shall be bathed in heaven and come down upon Idumea, the Greek and Roman name for Edom, America, France, Germany, Britain, Russia.
precepts.point: The fear of the Lord is all wisdom, Sirach 19:20, and in all wisdom is the performance of the law: be about it, not just talk about it. If you do not fear the Lord, that is where your problems are.
precepts.why:
Christ says it himself: “Immediately after the tribulation of those days.” People say there is no tribulation; there is going to be tribulation. Then “shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light”, as Luke read, “and the stars shall fall from heaven”: missiles. “and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken”: America, Britain, Germany, France, Russia, Canada, Spain, all those European nations, shaken with war.

How do we know the heavens are those nations? Isaiah 34: “And all the host of heaven shall be dissolved, and the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll: and all their host shall fall down, as the leaf falleth off from the vine”: bombs, nuclear bombs, missiles and satellites dropping out of the sky. “For my sword shall be bathed in heaven: behold, it shall come down upon Idumea.” Idumea is the Greek and Roman name for Edom: America, France, Germany, Britain, Russia. That is heaven.

“And then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven.” After the tribulation there is still war; so don't say there's war, we're going home tomorrow. Where is the great tribulation, Jacob's trouble?

“And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds.” He is not gathering everybody, only the elect: “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect.” The elect are the Israelites, not Baptists, Pentecostals, Muslims or Catholics. That is our hope amid destruction.

precepts.text: Antiochus, swelling with anger and speaking proudly that he would make Jerusalem a burying place of the Jews, was smitten by the God of Israel with a remediless pain of the bowels as soon as he spoke, ceased not from bragging and breathing out fire against the Jews, fell from his chariot and was carried violently, and worms rose out of his body while his flesh fell away and the stench sickened his whole army.
precepts.point: The people shall be as the burnings of lime, as thorns cut up burnt in the fire. Not the fire of 2 Kings: Isaiah 9:5, every battle of the warrior is with confused noise and garments rolled in blood, but this shall be with burning and fuel of fire, thermonuclear fire.
precepts.why:
“Now will I rise, saith the Lord; now will I be exalted; now will I lift up myself. Ye shall conceive chaff, ye shall bring forth stubble: your breath, as fire, shall devour you.” What does that mean, your breath as fire shall devour you? When you speak great words and talk big talk that you can't back up with God, you are going to eat your words. Like Nicanor pointing at the temple and saying we are going to tear it to the ground. Antiochus is the example.

“Then swelling with anger, he thought to avenge upon the Jews the disgrace done unto him by those that made him flee.” He commanded his chariotman to drive without ceasing, “the judgment of God now following him. For he had spoken proudly in this sort, That he would come to Jerusalem and make it a common burying place of the Jews.” He wanted to destroy us.

“But the Lord Almighty, the God of Isreal, smote him with an incurable and invisible plague.” As soon as he had spoken those words: that is what “your breath, as fire, shall devour you” means. “A pain of the bowels that was remediless came upon him, and sore torments of the inner parts; And that most justly: for he had tormented other men’s bowels with many and strange torments.” Good for him.

“Howbeit he nothing at all ceased from his bragging, but still was filled with pride, breathing out fire in his rage against the Jews.” There it is again, breathing out fire, the bottom of Isaiah 33:11: your big talk is going to burn you up. Then “he fell down from his chariot, carried violently”: he fell off the chariot and it dragged him. It was bad enough he had stomach pains; now his whole body hurt.

“And thus he that a little afore thought he might command the waves of the sea, (so proud was he beyond the condition of man) and weigh the high mountains in a balance, was now cast on the ground” … “So that the worms rose up out of the body of this wicked man” … “and the filthiness of his smell was noisome to all his army.” He began to stink worse than shit; his whole army could smell him.

That is what is coming to the nations talking big right now. America breaks the covenant and regards no man, and Israel broke the 2024 ceasefire and advanced into Lebanon saying they will silence Hezbollah by the end of the week. Their breath as fire shall devour them.

precepts.text: Every battle of the warrior is with confused noise and garments rolled in blood, but this shall be with burning and fuel of fire.
precepts.point: The people shall be as the burnings of lime, as thorns cut up burnt in the fire. Not the fire of 2 Kings: Isaiah 9:5, every battle of the warrior is with confused noise and garments rolled in blood, but this shall be with burning and fuel of fire, thermonuclear fire.
precepts.why:
Isaiah 33 ends: “And the people shall be as the burnings of lime: as thorns cut up shall they be burned in the fire.” There is going to be fire, but it is not the kind of fire we read about in 2 Kings, men being burnt up with fire from heaven in that way. Isaiah 9 shows what kind of fire it is.

“For every battle of the warrior is with confused noise, and garments rolled in blood.” That is how battles have always been fought: noise, confusion, men's garments rolled in blood.

“But this shall be with burning and fuel of fire.” This battle is going to be with fire. What kind of fire? Thermonuclear fire.

That is the fire of Isaiah 33, where Lebanon is ashamed and hewn down, Sharon, which is Tel Aviv, is like a wilderness, Bashan, which is Syria, and Carmel in northern Israel shake off their fruits. The highways lie waste, the wayfaring man ceases, and the valiant ones, the generals and armies, cry without. The people are burned like lime and like thorns cut up, and then the Lord says, “Hear, ye that are far off, what I have done; and, ye that are near, acknowledge my might.”

precepts.text: O Lord, righteousness belongeth unto thee, but unto us confusion of faces, to the men of Judah and all Israel near and far off, through all the countries whither thou hast driven them because of their trespass.
precepts.point: The hypocrites of our people: Isaiah 9:16-17, the leaders of this people cause them to err, the religious and political leaders, T.D. Jakes and Pastor P, and they that are led of them are destroyed; the Lord has no joy in their young men nor mercy on their fatherless and widows, for every one is an hypocrite and evil doer and every mouth speaketh folly. They all have the Bible and say they believe in Jesus and do not one word of it.
precepts.why:
“Hear, ye that are far off, what I have done; and, ye that are near, acknowledge my might.” Who are the far off? Daniel shows it's us.

“O Lord, righteousness belongeth unto thee, but unto us confusion of faces, as at this day.” The literal example: we were the top nation. Nations paid tribute to us under Solomon; David conquered everybody. Then we went into captivity, confused, and it was our sins that allowed it.

Bring it up to today. Our people go to school, get educated, get many degrees, and still are not accepted in this society. Now they are firing Black people with all those degrees: you're fired, we don't need you, DEI hire. And we say, but wait a minute, we did everything you told us to do. When we got away from them and built places like Black Wall Street and Seneca Village, they bombed us. They told us to fit in and get a good education; we did, and they still mock and scorn us. I assimilated, master, I'm one of you. That is confusion of faces.

“To the men of Judah, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and unto all Israel, that are near, and that are far off, through all the countries whither thou hast driven them.” Look at our people: Dominicans and Cubans saying I voted for Donald Trump, and now it is backfiring on them. They haven't been touched yet, but they are going to be touched.

“Because of their trespass that they have trespassed against thee.” That is why we are the far off, driven through all the countries, and why Isaiah calls on us to hear what the Lord has done and acknowledge his might.

precepts.text: I beheld till the thrones were cast down, and the Ancient of Days did sit, whose garment was white as snow and the hair of his head like pure wool; his throne was like the fiery flame and his wheels as burning fire; a fiery stream issued before him; thousand thousands ministered unto him; the judgment was set and the books opened; and the beast, America, was slain and given to the burning flame.
precepts.point: The hypocrites of our people: Isaiah 9:16-17, the leaders of this people cause them to err, the religious and political leaders, T.D. Jakes and Pastor P, and they that are led of them are destroyed; the Lord has no joy in their young men nor mercy on their fatherless and widows, for every one is an hypocrite and evil doer and every mouth speaketh folly. They all have the Bible and say they believe in Jesus and do not one word of it.
precepts.why:
“Who among us shall dwell with the devouring fire? who among us shall dwell with everlasting burnings?” What does it mean to dwell with fire? Daniel shows what it is to stand before the Lord in his kingdom.

“I beheld till the thrones were cast down.” Daniel looked in the vision and saw America fall, Britain, Germany, France, Canada and Australia fall, and China, Japan, North Korea and South Korea: all the powerful nations. “And the Ancient of days did sit”: having no beginning of days and no end of days, and in order to sit, you have to have a body. “Whose garment was white as snow”: to wear a garment you have to have a body. “And the hair of his head like the pure wool.” So what is God? A black man.

“His throne was like the fiery flame, and his wheels as burning fire.” His wheels are the chariots of heaven that they call UFOs. “A fiery stream issued and came forth from before him”: fire bursting from the throne at all times. You are not just rolling up on the Lord saying, Lord, I want to talk to you for a minute. You have to get through that fire first. This is going to be a kingdom of absolute order and rule.

“Thousand thousands ministered unto him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him: the judgment was set, and the books were opened. I beheld then because of the voice of the great words which the horn spake: I beheld even till the beast was slain, and his body destroyed, and given to the burning flame.” The horn speaking great words and the beast is America, slain and given to the burning flame.

That is the devouring fire and the everlasting burnings of Isaiah 33. The sinners in Zion are afraid of it, and only he that walketh righteously and speaketh uprightly shall dwell there.

precepts.text: The leaders of this people cause them to err, and they that are led of them are destroyed; the Lord shall have no joy in their young men nor mercy on their fatherless and widows, for every one is an hypocrite and an evildoer and every mouth speaketh folly.
precepts.point: The hypocrites of our people: Isaiah 9:16-17, the leaders of this people cause them to err, the religious and political leaders, T.D. Jakes and Pastor P, and they that are led of them are destroyed; the Lord has no joy in their young men nor mercy on their fatherless and widows, for every one is an hypocrite and evil doer and every mouth speaketh folly. They all have the Bible and say they believe in Jesus and do not one word of it.
precepts.why:
“The sinners in Zion are afraid; fearfulness hath surprised the hypocrites.” Zion is another name for Israel, and fearfulness will surprise the hypocrites of our people. Isaiah 9 gives the example.

“For the leaders of this people cause them to err.” These are the religious leaders and the political leaders of our people. Our leaders in this society cause us to err, cause us to sin, because we follow what they say and it is always against God. “And they that are led of them are destroyed.” You followed T.D. Jakes? You followed Pastor P and the other dudes on the screen? Destroyed.

“Therefore the Lord shall have no joy in their young men.” Because they follow foolish religious leaders and foolish political leaders. “Neither shall have mercy on their fatherless and widows”: God is not going to have mercy on the fatherless children and the widows whose husbands died.

“For every one is an hypocrite and an evildoer, and every mouth speaketh folly.” Every one of them is a hypocrite. They all have the Bible, they say they believe in Jesus, but they won't do nary a word in that book. Every mouth speaks lies; as soon as they open their black lips, it's a lie, and it isn't in the scriptures. “For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.”

Look at the churches: holy water and holy kisses, people falling out saying they have the Holy Spirit. That is why the racist white man says all the Black churches need to be shut down and come learn from the white man how to serve God. And now there are Israelites who know they are Israel speaking in tongues and calling it a heavenly language, bringing the lies of foolishness into this truth. Those are the hypocrites the fear will surprise.

precepts.text: When thou doest alms, sound not a trumpet as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and streets; when thou prayest, be not as the hypocrites who love to pray standing in the corners of the streets to be seen of men. They have their reward.
precepts.point: The hypocrites of our people: Isaiah 9:16-17, the leaders of this people cause them to err, the religious and political leaders, T.D. Jakes and Pastor P, and they that are led of them are destroyed; the Lord has no joy in their young men nor mercy on their fatherless and widows, for every one is an hypocrite and evil doer and every mouth speaketh folly. They all have the Bible and say they believe in Jesus and do not one word of it.
precepts.why:
When the Bible calls our people hypocrites, look at the hypocrisy. “Therefore when thou doest thine alms, do not sound a trumpet before thee, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, that they may have glory of men. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.” Christ was condemning the Pharisees, who gave their alms publicly and made a big announcement that they gave such an amount of money so everybody could see.

“But when thou doest alms, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth: That thine alms may be in secret: and thy Father which seeth in secret himself shall reward thee openly.”

Now look at Marvin Winans at Perfecting Church. A grandmother stands up to sow her seed of a thousand plus two hundred thirty-five dollars before everybody, and he embarrasses her: y'all not listening, I said a thousand plus a thousand. She says she'll work on the other eight hundred, and he says that ain't what I asked you to do, and the organ goes right on playing like it agreed. That is what the Pharisees were doing, sounding a trumpet in the synagogue.

“And when thou prayest, thou shalt not be as the hypocrites are: for they love to pray standing in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen of men. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.” And there are thousands praying in the streets in California to be seen: that is what Christ said not to do. Those are all Christians.

The Pharisees were our people, and the hypocrites of Isaiah 33 whom fearfulness will surprise are our people in these churches today, doing the very things Christ condemned.

precepts.text: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, for ye devour widows' houses and for a pretence make long prayer; ye shall receive the greater damnation. The pastor who kept the widow's check. Matthew 24:51, the unfaithful servant's portion is with the hypocrites, weeping and gnashing of teeth in the lake of fire, and the modern Pharisees are our people in Christianity.
precepts.point: The hypocrites of our people: Isaiah 9:16-17, the leaders of this people cause them to err, the religious and political leaders, T.D. Jakes and Pastor P, and they that are led of them are destroyed; the Lord has no joy in their young men nor mercy on their fatherless and widows, for every one is an hypocrite and evil doer and every mouth speaketh folly. They all have the Bible and say they believe in Jesus and do not one word of it.
precepts.why:
“Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye devour widows’ houses, and for a pretence make long prayer: therefore ye shall receive the greater damnation.” Christ is talking about the Pharisees being hypocrites, and the Pharisees were our people, devouring widows' houses.

Here it is today. Someone wrote a check to the church addressed to a widow, gave it to the pastor, and told him the money was for her. The pastor took the money, and the widow never knew. She only found out because the treasurer went back to thank the donor, and the donor said, no, that money was for them. Now there is a big falling out, and the pastor is trying to force the widow out of the church. These pastors are robbing widows. That is what Christ said the Pharisees do, and he is telling us, don't do that.

And their end: the unfaithful servant is cut asunder and given “his portion with the hypocrites: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.” That is the lake of fire when the Lord returns.

In that time he was talking about the Pharisees, but today the modern-day Pharisees are our people in Christianity. They do everything the Pharisees did. Those are the hypocrites Isaiah says fearfulness will surprise, when they ask who among us shall dwell with the devouring fire.

precepts.text: In the last days the mountain of the Lord's house shall be established in the top of the mountains and exalted above the hills, and all nations shall flow unto it, for out of Zion shall go forth the law. The munitions of rocks.
precepts.point: Jeremiah 46:27: fear not, O my servant Jacob, because Jacob's trouble and Armageddon are coming; I will save thee from afar off, this far-off land, and thy seed from the land of their captivity, and Jacob shall return and be in rest and at ease, and none shall make him afraid.
precepts.why:
Isaiah 33:16 says the one who walks righteously “shall dwell on high: his place of defence shall be the munitions of rocks”. His place of defence is the kingdom, and Isaiah 2 shows what the munitions of rocks are.

“And it shall come to pass in the last days, that the mountain of the Lord’s house shall be established in the top of the mountains, and shall be exalted above the hills”. The mountain of the Lord's house is the highest government on earth, literally. “and all nations shall flow unto it.”

“And many people shall go and say, Come ye, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for out of Zion shall go forth the law”. That is what goes forth out of Zion: the law.

So to dwell on high is to dwell in that kingdom, set above every other government, and that is the promise to the one who meets the stipulation of Isaiah 33:15. There, “bread shall be given him; his waters shall be sure.”

precepts.text: He hath on his vesture and on his thigh a name written, King of kings and Lord of lords. The King you will see in his beauty is Christ.
precepts.point: Jeremiah 46:27: fear not, O my servant Jacob, because Jacob's trouble and Armageddon are coming; I will save thee from afar off, this far-off land, and thy seed from the land of their captivity, and Jacob shall return and be in rest and at ease, and none shall make him afraid.
precepts.why:
“And he hath on his vesture and on his thigh a name written, KING OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS.” When Isaiah 33:17 says “Thine eyes shall see the king in his beauty”, it is talking about Christ. He is the King of kings; he is the Lord of lords.

Isaiah 33 asks who shall dwell with the devouring fire, who shall dwell with everlasting burnings before the Lord, and answers: he that walketh righteously and speaketh uprightly, speaking what the Bible says and living what it says; he that despiseth the gain of oppressions, the oppression you see as soon as you walk out these doors, which our brothers and sisters in the church make like they don't see; he that shaketh his hands from holding of bribes; he that stoppeth his ears from hearing of blood and shutteth his eyes from seeing evil. That one shall dwell on high.

And that one shall see the King. We want to see the Lord for ourselves, and the King we shall see in his beauty is Christ, with his name written on his vesture and on his thigh.

precepts.text: I know that my redeemer liveth and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth; and though after my skin worms destroy this body, yet in my flesh shall I see God, whom I shall see for myself, and mine eyes shall behold, and not another.
precepts.point: Jeremiah 46:27: fear not, O my servant Jacob, because Jacob's trouble and Armageddon are coming; I will save thee from afar off, this far-off land, and thy seed from the land of their captivity, and Jacob shall return and be in rest and at ease, and none shall make him afraid.
precepts.why:
Isaiah 33:17 says “Thine eyes shall see the king in his beauty”, and Job shows how. “For I know that my redeemer liveth”. Our redeemer is Christ, who sacrificed himself for our people, the twelve tribes of Israel. “and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth”: in the latter day our redeemer shall stand upon the earth.

“And though after my skin worms destroy this body, yet in my flesh shall I see God”. Job said, after my death, when worms destroy this body, yet in my flesh shall I see God. He knew he would be resurrected, regenerated, and we have to know that thing too. Although you die, you are going to be resurrected and regenerated, and that is when your eyes shall see the King in his beauty.

“Whom I shall see for myself, and mine eyes shall behold, and not another”. It is not going to be somebody else, and it is not only spiritual, as the Christians say, because Christians don't know the Bible. Job said, I'm going to be back for myself, and I'm going to behold the Lord with my own eyes, and not another, “though my reins be consumed within me”: though my body be destroyed.

precepts.text: Fear not, O my servant Jacob, and be not dismayed, O Israel, for I will save thee from afar off and thy seed from the land of their captivity, and Jacob shall return and be in rest and at ease, and none shall make him afraid.
precepts.point: Jeremiah 46:27: fear not, O my servant Jacob, because Jacob's trouble and Armageddon are coming; I will save thee from afar off, this far-off land, and thy seed from the land of their captivity, and Jacob shall return and be in rest and at ease, and none shall make him afraid.
precepts.why:
Isaiah 33:17 ends, “they shall behold the land that is very far off”, and that land is Jerusalem. Jeremiah shows how we get back to it.

“But fear not thou, O my servant Jacob, and be not dismayed, O Israel”. He says it because of great tribulation: Jacob's trouble will be coming. Tribulation leads into Armageddon. World War III has already begun, and in the middle of that will be Armageddon. So the Lord says, fear not, be not dismayed.

“for, behold, I will save thee from afar off”, because we have been taken captive into far off lands; here in America is a far off land. “and thy seed from the land of their captivity; and Jacob shall return, and be in rest and at ease”. We ain't going to be bothered by anybody; we shall be in rest and at ease. “and none shall make him afraid”: there is no nation that is going to make us afraid ever, ever again.

So the one whose eyes see the King in his beauty is also brought out of the far off land of his captivity to behold the land that is very far off, Jerusalem, and dwell there in rest.

precepts.text: The strong people shall glorify thee, the city of the terrible nations shall fear thee, for thou hast been a strength to the poor and needy, a refuge from the storm and a shadow from the heat; thou shalt bring down the noise of strangers, and the branch of the terrible ones shall be brought low.
precepts.point: Look upon Zion, the city of our solemnities; thine eyes shall see Jerusalem a quiet habitation, at rest, a tabernacle that shall not be taken down, not one stake removed nor any cord broken. You will never take down Jerusalem again. Psalms 46:4-7, God is in the midst of her, she shall not be moved; the heathen raged, the kingdoms were moved, he uttered his voice, the earth melted; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Psalms 48:1-2, beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, the city of the great King.
precepts.why:
Isaiah 33:19 says “Thou shalt not see a fierce people”, and Isaiah 25 shows why: those fierce nations will be subdued. “Therefore shall the strong people glorify thee, the city of the terrible nations shall fear thee.” The terrible nations, the ones that made everyone afraid, will themselves fear the Most High.

“For thou hast been a strength to the poor, a strength to the needy in his distress, a refuge from the storm, a shadow from the heat, when the blast of the terrible ones is as a storm against the wall.” That is us. Verse 4 is Israel: the poor and the needy that the terrible ones have been blasting against like a storm, and God has been our refuge through it.

“Thou shalt bring down the noise of strangers”, and that goes right back to verse 3: the city of the terrible nations shall fear. Then, “the branch of the terrible ones shall be brought low”: their branch, their people, brought low. So when Isaiah 33 says we shall not see that fierce people of a deeper speech and a stammering tongue, it is because God has brought them down.

precepts.text: Who shall not fear thee, O Lord? For all nations shall come and worship before thee, for thy judgments are made manifest.
precepts.point: Look upon Zion, the city of our solemnities; thine eyes shall see Jerusalem a quiet habitation, at rest, a tabernacle that shall not be taken down, not one stake removed nor any cord broken. You will never take down Jerusalem again. Psalms 46:4-7, God is in the midst of her, she shall not be moved; the heathen raged, the kingdoms were moved, he uttered his voice, the earth melted; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Psalms 48:1-2, beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, the city of the great King.
precepts.why:
“Who shall not fear thee, O Lord, and glorify thy name? for thou only art holy: for all nations shall come and worship before thee; for thy judgments are made manifest.” His judgments made manifest are his prophecies and his laws coming to pass before everyone's eyes.

This is why Isaiah 33:19 says “Thou shalt not see a fierce people.” When all nations come and worship before the Most High, they are no longer fierce against Israel. They are subdued. That is what the Lord is saying here: these nations will be brought down and made to come and worship before him.

So the fierce people of a deeper speech and a stammering tongue, the nations whose languages we cannot understand, will not be seen raging against us any more. They will be bowing before the King, because the Lord only is holy and all the nations will fear him.

precepts.text: Every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem shall go up from year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles. The nations will be forced to give up their idols.
precepts.point: Look upon Zion, the city of our solemnities; thine eyes shall see Jerusalem a quiet habitation, at rest, a tabernacle that shall not be taken down, not one stake removed nor any cord broken. You will never take down Jerusalem again. Psalms 46:4-7, God is in the midst of her, she shall not be moved; the heathen raged, the kingdoms were moved, he uttered his voice, the earth melted; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Psalms 48:1-2, beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, the city of the great King.
precepts.why:
Zechariah shows what it looks like when the nations are subdued: “every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem shall even go up from year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles.”

Those that are left are the ones who came against Jerusalem. These nations are going to be forced to give up their idols and come before the King. Year after year they must go up and keep the feast of tabernacles, the very feast they never kept.

That is why Isaiah 33:19 says “Thou shalt not see a fierce people.” The fierce nations with a stammering tongue will not be fierce any more; what is left of them will be worshipping the King, the Lord of hosts, at Jerusalem.

precepts.text: Arise, O Lord, let not man prevail; let the heathen be judged in thy sight. Put them in fear, O Lord, that the nations may know themselves to be but men. Selah.
precepts.point: Look upon Zion, the city of our solemnities; thine eyes shall see Jerusalem a quiet habitation, at rest, a tabernacle that shall not be taken down, not one stake removed nor any cord broken. You will never take down Jerusalem again. Psalms 46:4-7, God is in the midst of her, she shall not be moved; the heathen raged, the kingdoms were moved, he uttered his voice, the earth melted; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Psalms 48:1-2, beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, the city of the great King.
precepts.why:
“Arise, O Lord; let not man prevail”: let not man prevail against us. Then, “let the heathen be judged in thy sight”: let the heathen nations be judged in his sight. “Put them in fear, O Lord: that the nations may know themselves to be but men.” These nations must learn that they themselves are only men. “Selah”, meaning it is true.

Then read Isaiah 33:19 again: “Thou shalt not see a fierce people.” Why? Because they shall be subdued. It is “a people of a deeper speech than thou canst perceive; of a stammering tongue, that thou canst not understand”: that is the other nations, whose languages we do not know.

The nations have acted like gods over Israel. The Most High puts them in fear so they know they are but men, and then they are subdued and forced to worship the King. That is why we will not see that fierce people again.

precepts.text: There is a river whose streams make glad the city of God; God is in the midst of her, she shall not be moved; the heathen raged, the kingdoms were moved; the Lord of hosts is with us, the God of Jacob is our refuge.
precepts.point: Look upon Zion, the city of our solemnities; thine eyes shall see Jerusalem a quiet habitation, at rest, a tabernacle that shall not be taken down, not one stake removed nor any cord broken. You will never take down Jerusalem again. Psalms 46:4-7, God is in the midst of her, she shall not be moved; the heathen raged, the kingdoms were moved, he uttered his voice, the earth melted; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Psalms 48:1-2, beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, the city of the great King.
precepts.why:
Isaiah 33:20 says to look upon Zion and see Jerusalem “a quiet habitation, a tabernacle that shall not be taken down”. Habitation meaning at rest, at peace. Like a tent with stakes driven down, not one stake of Jerusalem shall ever be pulled up, and not one cord broken.

Psalms 46 says the same: “There is a river, the streams whereof shall make glad the city of God, the holy place of the tabernacles of the most High. God is in the midst of her; she shall not be moved: God shall help her, and that right early.”

“The heathen raged, the kingdoms were moved”: all the heathen nations, the same ones we read about in Isaiah 33:19, the fierce people of a deeper speech and a stammering tongue that we cannot understand. Their kingdoms shall be moved. And “he uttered his voice, the earth melted. The Lord of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Selah.” God is our refuge; it is true.

So the nations are moved, but Jerusalem is not. She shall not be moved, because God is in the midst of her.

precepts.text: Great is the Lord in the city of our God, in the mountain of his holiness; beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, the city of the great King.
precepts.point: Look upon Zion, the city of our solemnities; thine eyes shall see Jerusalem a quiet habitation, at rest, a tabernacle that shall not be taken down, not one stake removed nor any cord broken. You will never take down Jerusalem again. Psalms 46:4-7, God is in the midst of her, she shall not be moved; the heathen raged, the kingdoms were moved, he uttered his voice, the earth melted; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Psalms 48:1-2, beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, the city of the great King.
precepts.why:
“Great is the Lord, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, in the mountain of his holiness.” The mountain of his holiness is Jerusalem.

“Beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King.” This is the Zion that Isaiah 33:20 tells us to look upon: “Look upon Zion, the city of our solemnities.” It is the city of the great King, the joy of the whole earth.

So the quiet habitation Isaiah saw is not a small thing. It is the city where the Lord is greatly praised, beautiful for situation, and it will never be taken down again.

precepts.text: I was glad when they said unto me, let us go into the house of the Lord; if that makes you sigh, something is wrong with your spirit. Jerusalem is builded as a city that is compact together, the same length, breadth, and height as Revelation 21:16, twelve thousand furlongs by angelic measure, with walls garnished with twelve precious stones, the same stones as the high priest's breastplate in Exodus 28:15-21, engraved with the names of the twelve tribes, and twelve gates with the names of the tribes, Revelation 21:12, so the kingdom is not for everybody. Whither the tribes go up, the tribes of the Lord, not all nations, unto the testimony of Israel; for there are set thrones of judgment, the thrones of the house of David: Luke 22:30, ye shall sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes, and Revelation 20:4, they that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus and had not worshipped the beast nor his image nor received his mark, his lies in your mind, lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years.
precepts.point: Look upon Zion, the city of our solemnities; thine eyes shall see Jerusalem a quiet habitation, at rest, a tabernacle that shall not be taken down, not one stake removed nor any cord broken. You will never take down Jerusalem again. Psalms 46:4-7, God is in the midst of her, she shall not be moved; the heathen raged, the kingdoms were moved, he uttered his voice, the earth melted; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Psalms 48:1-2, beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, the city of the great King.
precepts.why:
“I was glad when they said unto me, Let us go into the house of the Lord.” That should make you glad. When somebody says, let's go up to the sanctuary, and you sigh, there is something wrong with your spirit. “Our feet shall stand within thy gates, O Jerusalem.”

“Jerusalem is builded as a city that is compact together”: the same height and the same width. Revelation 21 shows it: the city lieth foursquare, the length and the breadth and the height of it equal, measured by the angel, its foundations garnished with the same stones the high priest wore in Exodus 28, the stones with the names of the twelve tribes.

“Whither the tribes go up.” Wait a minute. Where all nations go up? No: whither the tribes go up, “the tribes of the Lord, unto the testimony of Israel, to give thanks unto the name of the Lord.” The testimony of Israel, because that kingdom is what was always prophesied. The kingdom is not for everybody.

“For there are set thrones of judgment, the thrones of the house of David.” Luke 22:30 shows those thrones, sitting on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel, and Revelation 20:4 shows who sits on them: the souls beheaded for the witness of Jesus, who had not worshipped the beast, the white man's kingdom, nor his image, his religion and his politics, nor received his mark, his lies in their foreheads, their minds. They live and reign with Christ a thousand years. This is the Jerusalem of Isaiah 33:20, the tabernacle that shall not be taken down.

precepts.text: A wall with twelve gates and the names of the twelve tribes; the city lieth foursquare, twelve thousand furlongs, length, breadth, and height equal, measured by the angel; the foundations garnished with jasper, sapphire, chalcedony, emerald, sardonyx, sardius, chrysolite, beryl, topaz, chrysoprasus, jacinth, and amethyst; twelve gates of pearl and the street of pure gold.
precepts.point: Look upon Zion, the city of our solemnities; thine eyes shall see Jerusalem a quiet habitation, at rest, a tabernacle that shall not be taken down, not one stake removed nor any cord broken. You will never take down Jerusalem again. Psalms 46:4-7, God is in the midst of her, she shall not be moved; the heathen raged, the kingdoms were moved, he uttered his voice, the earth melted; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Psalms 48:1-2, beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, the city of the great King.
precepts.why:
Psalms 122 says “Jerusalem is builded as a city that is compact together”, and Revelation 21 shows what that means: “the city lieth foursquare, and the length is as large as the breadth”, measured “with the reed, twelve thousand furlongs. The length and the breadth and the height of it are equal.” It is as tall as it is wide.

Twelve thousand furlongs is about 1,500 miles by man's measurement, but it is not man's measurement: “according to the measure of a man, that is, of the angel.” It is angelic measurement, so the size is not what we are thinking.

And “the building of the wall of it was of jasper: and the city was pure gold, like unto clear glass. And the foundations of the wall of the city were garnished with all manner of precious stones.” Garnished means decorated: all kinds of fancy designs in the walls of Jerusalem. Jasper, sapphire, chalcedony, emerald, sardonyx, sardius, chrysolite, beryl, topaz, chrysoprasus, jacinth, amethyst. Each stone represented one of the tribes, the same stones the high priest wore in Exodus 28. “And the twelve gates were twelve pearls”, “and the street of the city was pure gold, as it were transparent glass.”

And the city “had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel.” So the kingdom is not for everybody. This is the Zion Isaiah 33:20 tells us to look upon, the tabernacle that shall never be taken down.

precepts.text: The breastplate of judgment, foursquare and double like the city, with four rows of stones set in gold, and the stones with the names of the children of Israel, engraved like a signet, according to the twelve tribes.
precepts.point: Look upon Zion, the city of our solemnities; thine eyes shall see Jerusalem a quiet habitation, at rest, a tabernacle that shall not be taken down, not one stake removed nor any cord broken. You will never take down Jerusalem again. Psalms 46:4-7, God is in the midst of her, she shall not be moved; the heathen raged, the kingdoms were moved, he uttered his voice, the earth melted; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Psalms 48:1-2, beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, the city of the great King.
precepts.why:
The foundations of the kingdom of heaven are the same stones, the same gems, that the high priest wore. “And thou shalt make the breastplate of judgment with cunning work”: cunning work means make it look fancy. It has to be dope; it has to look good, not corny. It is made “of gold, of blue, and of purple, and of scarlet, and of fine twined linen, shalt thou make it.”

“Foursquare it shall be being doubled; a span shall be the length thereof, and a span shall be the breadth thereof.” It was designed like a square, the same height as it was wide, just like the kingdom, where the length and the breadth and the height are equal.

“And thou shalt set in it settings of stones, even four rows of stones”: sardius, topaz and carbuncle; emerald, sapphire and diamond; ligure, agate and amethyst; beryl, onyx and jasper. And “they shall be set in gold in their inclosings”, the gold holding them in.

“And the stones shall be with the names of the children of Israel, twelve, according to their names, like the engravings of a signet; every one with his name shall they be according to the twelve tribes.” These stones are the names of the children of Israel. Revelation 21 says the same thing about the kingdom of heaven: its foundations and its gates carry the twelve tribes. The Jerusalem of Isaiah 33:20 is built on Israel.

precepts.text: That ye may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
precepts.point: Look upon Zion, the city of our solemnities; thine eyes shall see Jerusalem a quiet habitation, at rest, a tabernacle that shall not be taken down, not one stake removed nor any cord broken. You will never take down Jerusalem again. Psalms 46:4-7, God is in the midst of her, she shall not be moved; the heathen raged, the kingdoms were moved, he uttered his voice, the earth melted; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Psalms 48:1-2, beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, the city of the great King.
precepts.why:
Psalms 122:5 says “For there are set thrones of judgment, the thrones of the house of David.” Christ tells his apostles where those thrones are: “That ye may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.”

The thrones in Jerusalem are thrones for judging the twelve tribes. That is why Psalms 122 says it is whither the tribes go up, the tribes of the Lord, unto the testimony of Israel, and not all nations.

So the quiet habitation of Isaiah 33:20, the city of our solemnities, is the seat of the kingdom, with Christ's table and the thrones of the house of David set in it.

precepts.text: I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them, the souls beheaded for the witness of Jesus who had not worshipped the beast nor his image nor received his mark, and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years.
precepts.point: Look upon Zion, the city of our solemnities; thine eyes shall see Jerusalem a quiet habitation, at rest, a tabernacle that shall not be taken down, not one stake removed nor any cord broken. You will never take down Jerusalem again. Psalms 46:4-7, God is in the midst of her, she shall not be moved; the heathen raged, the kingdoms were moved, he uttered his voice, the earth melted; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Psalms 48:1-2, beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, the city of the great King.
precepts.why:
“And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them”: the thrones of judgment of Psalms 122.

Then “I saw the souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God”: that is great tribulation. They are the ones “which had not worshipped the beast”: which had not worshipped this white man, this kingdom. Nor “his image”: his religion, his politics. And they had not “received his mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands”: they did not receive his lies in their foreheads, in their minds.

And so “they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years.” Those who come through great tribulation without bowing to the beast are the ones who sit on the thrones in the Jerusalem Isaiah 33:20 describes, the tabernacle that shall not be taken down.

precepts.text: I will bring my people again from Bashan and the depths of the sea, that thy foot may be dipped in the blood of thine enemies and the tongue of thy dogs in the same. They have seen thy goings, my King, in the sanctuary: singers before, players on instruments after, damsels with timbrels, beautiful songs, not like the churches. Little Benjamin with their ruler, almost wiped out and the baby tribe; the princes of Judah and their council, Zebulun, and Naphtali, the re-established kingdom. Because of thy temple at Jerusalem shall kings bring presents; rebuke the spearmen and the bulls, the powers of the nations, till every one submit himself with pieces of silver, tribute; scatter thou the people that delight in war, the white man, who renamed the Department of Defense the Department of War.
precepts.point: Look upon Zion, the city of our solemnities; thine eyes shall see Jerusalem a quiet habitation, at rest, a tabernacle that shall not be taken down, not one stake removed nor any cord broken. You will never take down Jerusalem again. Psalms 46:4-7, God is in the midst of her, she shall not be moved; the heathen raged, the kingdoms were moved, he uttered his voice, the earth melted; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Psalms 48:1-2, beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, the city of the great King.
precepts.why:
“The Lord said, I will bring again from Bashan, I will bring my people again from the depths of the sea.” Why bring them again? Because God's people are not in the holy land. “That thy foot may be dipped in the blood of thine enemies, and the tongue of thy dogs in the same.” Damn! Our foot shall be dipped in the blood of our enemies, and those nations that run their mouths against us, the same with them.

“They have seen thy goings, O God; even the goings of my God, my King, in the sanctuary.” That is the sanctuary. “The singers went before, the players on instruments followed after; among them were the damsels playing with timbrels.” People singing before the Lord, not like these churches: beautiful songs, with men and women behind them playing instruments and young girls with timbrels. “Bless ye God in the congregations, even the Lord, from the fountain of Israel.” The fountain of Israel is Christ.

“There is little Benjamin with their ruler, the princes of Judah and their council, the princes of Zebulun, and the princes of Naphtali.” Little Benjamin because they almost got wiped out, and they are the youngest tribe, the baby tribe. This is his re-established kingdom.

“Because of thy temple at Jerusalem shall kings bring presents unto thee”: tribute. “Rebuke the company of spearmen”, the soldiers, “the multitude of the bulls”, the people that have power in the other nations, “with the calves of the people”, their little ones, “till every one submit himself with pieces of silver”: till every nation submits and brings us tribute. Then, “scatter thou the people that delight in war.” You know who that is? The white man. If there is no war, he will make one; if there is peace on earth, he will undo it. They changed the Department of Defense to the Department of War. They delight in war.

This is the Jerusalem of Isaiah 33:20: the temple standing, the tribes gathered, the kings bringing tribute, and the fierce nations subdued.

precepts.text: Deliver me from the evil man, preserve me from the violent man, which imagine mischiefs in their heart; continually are they gathered together for war, from Venezuela to Iran to Mexico and Cuba. They have sharpened their tongues like a serpent, mocking Spain for refusing them; adders' poison, their philosophies and politics, is under their lips. Keep me from the hands of the wicked, who have purposed to overthrow my goings; the proud have hid a snare and spread a net and set gins for me. Selah.
precepts.point: Look upon Zion, the city of our solemnities; thine eyes shall see Jerusalem a quiet habitation, at rest, a tabernacle that shall not be taken down, not one stake removed nor any cord broken. You will never take down Jerusalem again. Psalms 46:4-7, God is in the midst of her, she shall not be moved; the heathen raged, the kingdoms were moved, he uttered his voice, the earth melted; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Psalms 48:1-2, beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, the city of the great King.
precepts.why:
Psalms 140 proves who the people are that delight in war. “Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man: preserve me from the violent man.” Psalms 68 said scatter the nations that delight in war; don't you see Trump and them delighting in war?

“Which imagine mischiefs in their heart; continually are they gathered together for war.” You thought it would end with Venezuela. Oh, no. He said we are going to hit Iran. You thought it ended there; next week Mexico, and maybe Cuba. The party is not over.

“They have sharpened their tongues like a serpent”: the things they say. Don't you hear them mocking the nations? They wanted to land in Spain, Spain said no, and now they are mad and talking about Spain. And “adders’ poison is under their lips”: their philosophies, their religions, their politics. “Selah”, meaning it is true.

“Keep me, O Lord, from the hands of the wicked”: this so-called white man, keep me from their hands. Then, “preserve me from the violent man; who have purposed to overthrow my goings.” They purposed to overthrow the goings of the children of Israel. “The proud have hid a snare for me, and cords; they have spread a net by the wayside; they have set gins for me. Selah.” Traps all around.

These are the fierce nations of Isaiah 33:19. When the Lord scatters them, we shall not see that fierce people any more, and Jerusalem will be a quiet habitation.

precepts.text: Gilead is mine, Manasseh is mine, Ephraim is the strength of mine head; Judah is my lawgiver.
precepts.point: The inhabitant shall not say, I am sick; the people that dwell therein shall be forgiven their iniquity. Psalms 103:1-4, bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits, who forgiveth all thine iniquities, who healeth all thy diseases, who redeemeth thy life from destruction.
precepts.why:
Isaiah says, “For the Lord is our judge, the Lord is our lawgiver, the Lord is our king; he will save us.” The Lord is our judge, not the nations. And the Lord is our lawgiver. Brothers used to get confused over this, so David shows which tribe the lawgiver comes from: “Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine; Ephraim also is the strength of mine head; Judah is my lawgiver”.

You would think it is supposed to be Levi, the priestly tribe. It says Judah. Why? Because the Lord who is our lawgiver came out of Judah, as Hebrews 7:14 shows. Christ is the lawgiver: he is the one that gave Moses the laws, and he is from Judah.

precepts.text: It is evident that our Lord sprang out of Judah, of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood. Christ from Judah is the lawgiver.
precepts.point: The inhabitant shall not say, I am sick; the people that dwell therein shall be forgiven their iniquity. Psalms 103:1-4, bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits, who forgiveth all thine iniquities, who healeth all thy diseases, who redeemeth thy life from destruction.
precepts.why:
Psalm 60 says “Judah is my lawgiver”, when you would expect it to say Levi. Hebrews gives the reason: “For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood.”

So Christ is the lawgiver. He comes from the tribe of Judah, and he is the one that gave Moses the laws. That is the Lord Isaiah speaks of: “the Lord is our judge, the Lord is our lawgiver, the Lord is our king; he will save us.” Our judge, our lawgiver and our king is Christ out of Judah, and it is he who will save us when the warships and navies of the nations come down.

precepts.text: Sing with gladness for Jacob and shout among the chief of the nations; O Lord, save thy people, the remnant of Israel. I will bring them from the north country and gather them from the coasts of the earth, with them the blind and the lame, the woman with child; they shall come with weeping, and I will lead them by rivers of waters in a straight way, for I am a father to Israel and Ephraim is my firstborn.
precepts.point: The inhabitant shall not say, I am sick; the people that dwell therein shall be forgiven their iniquity. Psalms 103:1-4, bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits, who forgiveth all thine iniquities, who healeth all thy diseases, who redeemeth thy life from destruction.
precepts.why:
Isaiah says “then is the prey of a great spoil divided; the lame take the prey.” Who is the lame? Jeremiah shows it: “For thus saith the Lord; Sing with gladness for Jacob, and shout among the chief of the nations: publish ye, praise ye, and say, O Lord, save thy people, the remnant of Israel.” The Lord is not saving all Israelites; he is saving a remnant.

“Behold, I will bring them from the north country, and gather them from the coasts of the earth, and with them the blind and the lame”. The blind and the lame are Israel, with “the woman with child and her that travaileth with child together: a great company shall return thither.”

“They shall come with weeping, and with supplications will I lead them: I will cause them to walk by the rivers of waters in a straight way, wherein they shall not stumble: for I am a father to Israel, and Ephraim is my firstborn.” Ephraim is the firstborn, meaning he was chosen over the northern kingdom.

So the lame that take the prey is Israel. When the tacklings of their ships are loosed and they cannot spread the sail, we are going to take the nations: we are going to prey on the nations.

precepts.text: The multitude wondered when they saw the dumb to speak, the maimed to be whole, the lame to walk, and the blind to see, and they glorified the God of Israel.
precepts.point: The inhabitant shall not say, I am sick; the people that dwell therein shall be forgiven their iniquity. Psalms 103:1-4, bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits, who forgiveth all thine iniquities, who healeth all thy diseases, who redeemeth thy life from destruction.
precepts.why:
Isaiah says “the lame take the prey. And the inhabitant shall not say, I am sick”. Jeremiah 31 showed the lame is Israel, and Christ shows the lame being made whole: “Insomuch that the multitude wondered, when they saw the dumb to speak, the maimed to be whole, the lame to walk, and the blind to see: and they glorified the God of Israel.”

The dumb speak, the maimed are whole, the lame walk and the blind see, and they glorified the God of Israel. That is the lame of Isaiah 33. The lame take the prey: we are going to take the nations and divide the spoil, and in that day the inhabitants of Jerusalem will never say, I am sick.

precepts.text: Bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits: who forgiveth all thine iniquities, who healeth all thy diseases, who redeemeth thy life from destruction, who crowneth thee with lovingkindness and tender mercies.
precepts.point: The inhabitant shall not say, I am sick; the people that dwell therein shall be forgiven their iniquity. Psalms 103:1-4, bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits, who forgiveth all thine iniquities, who healeth all thy diseases, who redeemeth thy life from destruction.
precepts.why:
Isaiah ends, “And the inhabitant shall not say, I am sick: the people that dwell therein shall be forgiven their iniquity.” Nobody is going to be saying they are sick. David shows why: “Bless the Lord, O my soul: and all that is within me, bless his holy name. Bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits”.

Watch the benefits: “Who forgiveth all thine iniquities; who healeth all thy diseases; Who redeemeth thy life from destruction; who crowneth thee with lovingkindness and tender mercies”. The same Lord who forgives all our iniquities heals all our diseases, and the Lord can redeem our life from destruction.

That is the hope amid destruction. While the indignation of the Lord is upon all nations and his fury upon all their armies, the people that dwell in Jerusalem are forgiven their iniquity and healed, never to say I am sick again.
