precepts.text: When Israel keeps the law they shall not see a fierce people of a deeper, stammering speech they cannot understand.
precepts.point: With stammering lips and another tongue He will speak to this people; off the slave ships Israel spoke different languages, and because they did not keep the law the oppressor's culture was beaten into them until they came to understand. This Bible is the rest and the refreshing, yet they would not hear, so the word came precept upon precept that they might fall backward and be broken and snared.

note.label: Isaiah 28: Woe to the Drunkards of Ephraim and Precept Upon Precept

precepts.why:
“For with stammering lips and another tongue will he speak to this people.” Isaiah 33 shows the other side of it: “Thou shalt not see a fierce people, a people of a deeper speech than thou canst perceive; of a stammering tongue, that thou canst not understand.” When Israel keeps the law, they shall not see that fierce people with the deeper, stammering speech they cannot understand.

So the stammering lips and another tongue of Isaiah 28 are a punishment for not keeping the law. Off the slave ships Israel spoke different languages, and because they did not keep the law, the oppressor’s culture was beaten into them until they came to understand. Keep the law and you do not see that fierce people; break it and their tongue is what you hear.

precepts.text: King David quiets himself as a weaned child and says, "Let Israel hope in the Lord from henceforth and for ever."
precepts.point: "O Lord, be gracious unto us; we have waited for thee" is again the cry of patience. As Passover approaches spirits can get shaky, so the word is brought to heal you and remind you that when you go through trials your faith is being tested, the way Ecclesiasticus 2 must be applied.

note.label: Isaiah 33: The Lord Our Judge, Lawgiver, and King

precepts.why:
“O Lord, be gracious unto us; we have waited for thee: be thou their arm every morning, our salvation also in the time of trouble.” It is again the cry of patience, and King David shows how to carry it: “Lord, my heart is not haughty, nor mine eyes lofty: neither do I exercise myself in great matters, or in things too high for me. Surely I have behaved and quieted myself, as a child that is weaned of his mother: my soul is even as a weaned child. Let Israel hope in the Lord from henceforth and for ever.”

King David quiets himself as a weaned child, not haughty, not reaching into things too high for him, and says, “Let Israel hope in the Lord from henceforth and for ever.” As Passover approaches spirits can get shaky, so the word is brought to heal you and remind you that when you go through trials your faith is being tested, the way Ecclesiasticus 2 must be applied. Quiet yourself, wait for him, and hope in the Lord; he is our salvation in the time of trouble.

precepts.text: Know how to behave in the house of God, the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth.
precepts.point: We are the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth, and we must learn to behave ourselves and possess our vessels, constrained from sin.

note.label: Isaiah 33: The Lord Our Judge, Lawgiver, and King

precepts.why:
“And wisdom and knowledge shall be the stability of thy times, and strength of salvation”. Paul tells Timothy where that comes from: “But continue thou in the things which thou hast learned and hast been assured of, knowing of whom thou hast learned them; And that from a child thou hast known the holy scriptures, which are able to make thee wise unto salvation through faith which is in Christ Jesus.”

The holy scriptures make you wise unto salvation, the very wisdom that is the stability of thy times and the strength of salvation. We are the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth, and we must know how to behave in the house of God. Continue in the things you have learned, knowing of whom you learned them, and learn to behave yourselves and possess your vessels.

precepts.text: The love of Christ constraineth us from sin.
precepts.point: We are the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth, and we must learn to behave ourselves and possess our vessels, constrained from sin.

note.label: Isaiah 33: The Lord Our Judge, Lawgiver, and King

precepts.why:
The Most High “hath filled Zion with judgment and righteousness”, and we who are the church of the living God must learn to behave ourselves and possess our vessels. What holds us back from sin? “For the love of Christ constraineth us; because we thus judge, that if one died for all, then were all dead”.

The love of Christ constraineth us from sin. Because he died for all, we judge that we were all dead, and so we are held in, constrained, from the sin that made us dead. That constraint is the fear of the Lord that is his treasure, and it is how we possess our vessels as the pillar and ground of the truth.

precepts.text: Wisdom is the keeping of the statutes and judgments the Most High commanded.
precepts.point: We are the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth, and we must learn to behave ourselves and possess our vessels, constrained from sin.

note.label: Isaiah 33: The Lord Our Judge, Lawgiver, and King

precepts.why:
“And wisdom and knowledge shall be the stability of thy times”. Wisdom and knowledge are the commandments: “Behold, I have taught you statutes and judgments, even as the Lord my God commanded me, that ye should do so in the land whither ye go to possess it.”

Wisdom is the keeping of the statutes and judgments the Most High commanded through Moses, to be done in the land. That is what he filled Zion with, judgment and righteousness, and that is what makes a people stable. Keep the statutes and judgments, and wisdom and knowledge are the stability of your times and the strength of salvation.

precepts.text: The priest's lips should keep knowledge, and the people seek the law at his mouth.
precepts.point: We are the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth, and we must learn to behave ourselves and possess our vessels, constrained from sin.

note.label: Isaiah 33: The Lord Our Judge, Lawgiver, and King

precepts.why:
Wisdom and knowledge are the commandments, and they are kept in a certain place: “For the priest’s lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of the Lord of hosts.”

The priest’s lips should keep knowledge, and the people seek the law at his mouth, because he is the messenger of the Lord of hosts. So the knowledge that is “the stability of thy times” is the law, kept on the priest’s lips and sought there by the people. That is how the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth, learns to behave itself: seeking the law at the mouth of the one who keeps it, in the fear of the Lord that is his treasure.

precepts.text: Wisdom and knowledge shall be the stability of thy times, keeping us stabilized and focused for what is coming.
precepts.point: This is the true meaning of loving your enemies. Christianity twists it to mean love the ones who enslaved, raped, and colonized your ancestors, stole your nationality, land, and heritage, miseducated you, gave you a false image of God, and today shut down anyone who says Israel is the true children of God. That is not the enemy the scripture means. The Bible means love the enemies within your own nation, because Paul, who persecuted and killed the disciples, was one of those enemies who could still repent.
precepts.why:
“And wisdom and knowledge shall be the stability of thy times, and strength of salvation: the fear of the Lord is his treasure.” Wisdom and knowledge are what keep us stabilized and focused for what is coming.

A man like Saul, with authority from the chief priests to bind all that call on the name, will rise again, even a pastor putting us to death. Wisdom and knowledge keep us steady through it: judge nothing before the time, love the enemies within your own nation, and know that anyone can repent.
